narr: Two voices on one front page this morning. The IRGC Navy commander, Ali Ozmaei, on social media: the US 'terrorist army's' Saildrone 5838 was struck; 'the Strait of Hormuz is blocked and under our intelligence supervision and smart control. Any hostile movement will be targeted.' Rezaei (SNSC secretary) on the IAEA vote: 'illegal, technically unfounded, entirely political' — 'politicised & disruptive actions will push countries toward withdrawing from the NPT'. And the Foreign Ministry: Araghchi spoke again with Faisal bin Farhan — 'continued cooperation and diplomatic efforts to prevent the conflict from widening' — and with Pakistan's Munir and South Korea's Cho. Pezeshkian at BRICS calls the bloc 'a tool against US pressure'. Nothing from Tehran on Khasab or on the FT's Salalah report; no NPT step taken; the freight-charge suspension stands.

Quiet overnight. A US official to Reuters, contradicting Trump's 'no damage': the Sep 8 salvo on Muwaffaq Salti left an A-10 without a wing and ~8 F-15s lightly damaged, and about thirty Patriots were fired at it — CSIS puts the remaining Patriot stock under 850 of 2,330. At the Council's Yemen session Washington 'stands firmly with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia' and calls the Houthis 'agents and tools of Iran'; a White House official says the US is 'empowering' Riyadh and Aden, not committing forces. Bessent's 'large' bank is still Monday's promise. The WSJ adds that Iran is assembling ballistic missiles underground again, in smaller numbers. CENTCOM: silent since Sep 8 — three days without a word on Khasab, the Saildrone, Sirik or the Sep 9 wave. Nothing yet from Washington on the Salalah meeting.
Reuters via Times of Israel · Arab News · WSJ · CENTCOM · Sep 11

No new rung; the first diplomatic move in a week instead. The FT (Reuters could not verify) says Gulf foreign ministers meet Araghchi in Salalah on Monday to win buy-in for an Oman–Iran temporary arrangement to manage Hormuz shipping — and Araghchi's second call with Faisal bin Farhan in a week is confirmed by both sides. Scored once, under the Oman strait-regime rule; the 'talks contact' nudge moves the 60-day odds to 52 force / 23 grind / 15 deal, and the two Gulf pots ease a tenth on the mediation component (Small Gulf 8.0, Saudi–UAE 7.3) — the full step waits for the meeting to convene. Against it: Ozmaei calls the strait 'blocked' and promises to target 'any hostile movement', Khasab is still unnamed 35 hours on, and Kpler counted 7 transits Thursday. Brent $106.2 after a 12% week; diesel above $6; AIS 24 h 13 in / 10 out. Live 06:00 UTC: a USAF KC-135R and a KC-46-class tanker over the UAE coast and Gulf of Oman, nothing over Iran. The dial: 84° / 84° / 87° / 82°.
FT via Reuters · Mehr · UKMTO · Kpler · TE · adsb.lol · Sep 11

UKMTO Warning 133-26 (19:10 UTC Sep 10): a master 4 nm west of Khasab, Oman — the Musandam side of the strait's mouth — reported four unknown projectiles hitting two unknown vessels, fire aboard one. Thirty-five hours on (06:00 UTC Sep 11): still no names, flags, types or casualties; UKMTO 'has not attributed the attack'; no IRGC claim, no Omani statement, no CENTCOM word. Kpler still counted 7 transits Thursday (5 in / 2 out). Same water as the Aug 31 and Sep 1 hits. Set as rung 5 at 15:00, actor Iran by pattern; if a tanker is named the 'tanker seized or fired on' nudge fires (+3 force). The longer the identities stay dark, the more this looks like small craft or dhows rather than a tanker — watch Windward's Friday brief and Lloyd's List.
Iran: force escalation early · tanker for tanker
NYT · WSJ · Times of Israel · TRT World · Fox · Trading Economics

Two insider reports in one day. The WSJ: Vance, Rubio and other top officials privately told Trump the war could last past January 2029. The New York Times (more than half a dozen officials): Vance bypassed the Pentagon in spring and summer to call commanders in the Middle East, Europe and Asia — objectives, tactics, casualty estimates, what Iran would do in the strait — and was told critical munitions are 'at their lowest levels ever', Patriot interceptors critically low, with worries about deterrence against China and Russia; Ratcliffe gave him direct access to CIA analysts and ONI writes him a daily Hormuz transit report. The Pentagon (Parnell): done with Trump's and Hegseth's knowledge. Trump on Fox tonight: 'I don't believe in the word regret'. Scored under the interceptor-constraint rule (favours Squeeze & hold / Deal); the '2029' line stays unscored. Brent closed $107.63 (+6.3%) on the day.
US: squeeze & hold vs escalate to win by Nov 3 — the munitions floor is now on the record
Bloomberg TV · Jerusalem Post · Times of Israel · Mehr · Trump · CSIS

Grossi is on the record: satellite imagery shows construction activity at Pickaxe Mountain (Kuh-e Kolang) south of Natanz; inspectors have not been inside. CSIS: internal construction, 'not yet capable of enrichment'. Trump: 'we may have to give them a shot there, too'. Tonight Netanyahu: Iran 'is attempting to rearm with nuclear weapons' after earlier operations 'degraded' it, and Israel is preparing for an Iranian escalation over Rosh Hashanah (Sep 11–13) with no specific warning. Iran's 11-page note calls the agency 'an instrument of war'. Board vote → DG finding → president naming the target → Israeli PM naming the rearmament: the permission structure for a Pickaxe strike is now four parts.
US: escalate to win by Nov 3 · bomb Pickaxe Mountain
Al Jazeera (Sanaa, New York) · Times of Israel · Reuters · gCaptain · Pakistan's UN mission

The Houthis hold Mocha and are moving toward Dhubab on Bab al-Mandeb and the Hanish Islands; the HOCC: the Red Sea is 'safe for all shipping except Saudi vessels'. Tonight the Security Council sat on Yemen: Saudi Arabia's al-Wasil — 'all necessary measures to deter Houthi attacks', end the 'support enabling' them; Pakistan's Ahmad — 'complete solidarity' with Riyadh, 'preserve the space for diplomacy'; Yemen's al-Saadi — the Houthis 'export the cost of the pressures facing Iran'. The Times of Israel: US military advisers in Saudi Arabia are assisting the strikes with intelligence and targeting (single source). Kpler: 6 Bab al-Mandeb transits Thursday vs ~30 a day. Not a Hormuz rung; the 'Houthis close the Red Sea' card is live — no rule scored until a ship is attacked.
Widen the war · Houthis close the Red Sea · Saudi front reopens with US help
Bloomberg · The National / Kpler · Trading Economics · PortWatch · FRED

Saudi August output 6.238 mb/d, the lowest since 1990, exports at a 13-year low; Kpler counts 2 large Hormuz transits Thursday after 9 Wednesday (the month's low) with 514 commercial ships stuck inside the Gulf, most sailing dark; PortWatch's week to Sep 6 is 3.1 large ships a day. Brent $108.9, WTI $103.9, the 10-yr 4.97 on an energy-driven PPI; Fed custody −$11.1B this week to $2,590.1B. Acled: US forces struck more tankers in the past week than in the previous four months (10 vs 12). The Saudi pot's revenue component is a judgment input — this print argues it is understated.
Saudi–UAE: forced to escalate · US: door shut (oil economics)
FT via Reuters · Arab News · Jerusalem Post · Mehr (Araghchi–Faisal) · Asharq Al-Awsat · Yonhap via Al Jazeera

The first diplomatic move in a week. The Financial Times (two people briefed; Reuters 'could not immediately verify') reports Gulf foreign ministers will meet Araghchi in Salalah, Oman, on Monday Sep 14 — an Oman–Iran push to secure Gulf buy-in for a temporary arrangement to manage shipping through the strait. Around it: Araghchi's second call in a week with Faisal bin Farhan (both sides confirm — 'continued cooperation and diplomacy to prevent the conflict from widening'), calls with Pakistan's Munir and South Korea's Cho (Seoul weighing a Hormuz deployment after a survey team returned from the UAE). What it is: the MOU track Iran wants (Iran's want #1: a strait regime it co-writes with Oman) meeting the Gulf's want (no toll, no Iranian control). What it is not: a US–Iran channel, and not yet a meeting. Tells before Monday: which capitals confirm attendance (Riyadh, Abu Dhabi, Doha, Kuwait); whether the IRGC's 'blocked' language softens; whether Washington blesses or dismisses it. Scored once under the Oman strait-regime rule; talks-contact nudge applied.
Iran: deal via Oman · MOU track — Gulf: Abu Dhabi/Riyadh opening a channel

The Axis line, morning of Sep 11: IRGC Navy commander Ali Ozmaei — Saildrone hull 5838 'struck'; 'the Strait of Hormuz is blocked and under our intelligence supervision and smart control. Any hostile movement will be targeted.' Rezaei (SNSC): the IAEA's 'politicised & disruptive actions will push countries toward withdrawing from the NPT' — the NPT-withdrawal marker Sam is watching, as a warning about 'countries', not a step by Iran. Mehr keeps the Saildrone video, 'rapid offensive operations' and Yemen 'close to full control of al-Makha' on top; the Saildrone claim is still single-source, CENTCOM silent three days (rung 8 at most if confirmed — not set). Against it, the same front page carries Araghchi's calls to Riyadh, Rawalpindi and Seoul. Rung 9 stays unset.
Iran: force escalation early · widen the war — blockade language while the FM phones the Gulf
The National · Mehr (TASS/Nebenzia) · Arab News · UN Meetings Coverage

The Council, two days after the 23–3–8 Board vote: still no session scheduled on the referral and no draft tabled; the UK and US are pushing to give the 1737 Committee a chair and a working panel of experts (mandate Sep 26) — Nebenzia: Moscow 'won't allow sanctions on Tehran to be reimposed under any circumstances', 'stop adding fuel to the fire'; China opposed the push (no quote). Thursday night's emergency session (UK/Bahrain) was on the Houthis, not Iran's file — Washington 'stands firmly' with Riyadh; Beijing 'concerned' but would not name the Houthis. Tehran's answer is words: Rezaei's NPT warning, Gharibabadi's 'will get nowhere'. Washington states no intent to act alone; the private evidence (WSJ '2029', NYT munitions, Reuters ~30 Patriots on one salvo, CSIS <850 left) keeps pulling toward the no-military-option reading.
